gaps: No demographic source counts food-delivery couriers; all of the above are resident/commuter proxies and cannot be used alone (per the known past error).

DTLA resident headcount is boundary-dependent: snippets give 61k-65k for vendor polygons, while the DTLA Alliance cites 100,000 residential units for its broader district; the BID's full demographic study and the LA City Planning Downtown profile (403) were not opened, so no boundary-explicit DTLA population was captured.

Car ownership (vehicles per household / zero-vehicle share) and commute mode for Koreatown, Westlake, Pico-Union, USC/University Park, Arts District, Little Tokyo were NOT captured this pass; they require pulling ACS tract tables (B08201/B25044, B08301) and aggregating to Mapping L.A. or community-plan polygons.
LA Times Mapping L.A. site is blocked to the fetcher; its polygons would have to be reconstructed from tract lists or a scraped GeoJSON.
Arts District and Little Tokyo are not separate Mapping L.A. neighborhoods (likely inside its 'Downtown' polygon) - confirmation and a sub-DTLA breakdown need tract or block-group work.
Latest official SF neighborhood profile PDF found is ACS 2012-2016; a current SF-core benchmark needs tract aggregation over the DataSF Analysis Neighborhoods layer.
No shared e-scooter trip data after Feb 2020 was found; LADOT MDS-based data may exist but was not located.
Metro Bike Share station-level trip totals around 768 Ceres were not computed (data exists; needs download and radius join).
Parking cost/scarcity evidence is from listing aggregators and marketing blogs only; no official LADOT meter-rate or occupancy study was captured.
Daytime population / employment and restaurant density in each zone belong to other modalities and were not scoped here.
must_ask_hmp: Home and work ZIP/neighborhood for the 300+ SF battery-rental subscribers, ~100 whole-vehicle renters, and the 1,000+ buyers, so the 'SF core zone' in the benchmark ratio matches where customers actually come from rather than an assumed SoMa/Mission/TL/FiDi polygon.
Distribution of distance riders travel to the SF shop for swaps and repairs (sets the defensible catchment radius to apply around 768 Ceres Ave).
Whether SF riders live inside the delivery zone or commute in from elsewhere (needed to decide if resident demographics are even the right proxy).
Share of HMP riders who own a car / have household vehicle access (public car-ownership data covers residents, not couriers).
Hour-of-day and day-of-week pattern of swaps/visits in SF (to judge night-time operation on the Skid Row edge in the site evaluation).
Any existing LA customer list or LA-origin web/Shopify orders (ZIP codes) as a direct demand signal.
surprises: Site ZIP 90021 has only 2,897 residents (ACS 2024 5-yr) at 1,465/sq mi - the depot sits in a near-empty industrial pocket; the rider population must come from adjacent ZIPs (Skid Row/Arts District 90013, Little Tokyo 90012, Fashion District 90015, Boyle Heights 90033).

DTLA population snippets (65,211 / 61,000) are BELOW the prior 80-90k, yet the DTLA Alliance's 100,000 residential units implies a far larger figure for its wider boundary - the prior number is not wrong so much as boundary-undefined.

Koreatown figure derived from Mapping L.A. (124,281 in 2008, 2.7 sq mi) is above the prior ~110k+; and Westlake is reported at 116,376 (2024, unverified), i.e. roughly Koreatown-sized and closer to 768 Ceres than Koreatown - Westlake may deserve equal weight.

DTLA Alliance survey: 46% of DTLA residents drive alone to work and 23% work from home; only 23% walk/bike/transit - resident car reliance is higher than the 'cars are disadvantaged' prior would suggest (caveat: residents, not couriers).
